previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and recently treated high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was readmitted for nausea, dehydration, and pancytopenia following her first cycle of adjuvant doxorubicin and cisplatin chemotherapy. She presented with fatigue, poor appetite, watery diarrhea, and a dry cough. Admission labs revealed acute kidney injury, low white blood cell and platelet counts, and elevated liver enzymes. She was managed with IV fluids, which resolved the dehydration and improved renal function, and received a red blood cell transfusion for symptomatic anemia. Her neutropenia was profound despite prior Neulasta, and a sore throat was attributed to viral pharyngitis with negative strep and blood cultures. Infectious workup showed past EBV and CMV exposure without active infection. A chest X-ray raised concern for early pneumonia, but her cough remained mild and stable without antibiotic treatment. Hepatology evaluated her chronic hepatitis C and transaminitis. For future cycles, Neulasta was switched to Neupogen for better control of white count recovery, and hydroxyurea was held. She improved clinically, with counts trending upward, and was discharged home with instructions on infection prevention, hydration, and close outpatient follow-up.

tolerated your chemotherapy well except for mild nausea and dry
